Subject: Acme - follow-up: usage & rate-limit clarification

Hi John —

Great talking earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: ~400M (range discussed: 200M–1B)
- Burst behavior: traffic can spike up to ~2x baseline for short windows (minutes-hours) during product launches
- Procurement/budget: target monthly budget in the $8k–$20k range; target unit economics mentioned ~ $10–$15 per 1M tokens
- Key asks: confirmation on burst capacity handling, quota increase process, and overage rates/terms

Ask from Redwood: can you confirm your typical peak window (minutes vs hours) and any hard SLOs around tail latency for interactive flows? That’ll help Camila size quota and recommend hosted vs Dedicated.

I attached a short pricing illustration with example scenarios (baseline vs burst) for reference.

Next steps:
1) John — confirm peak window length and whether bursts are predictable (e.g., launches) or random.
2) Camila — can you validate rate-limit options and overage tiers for the volumes above?
3) Marissa — I’ll prepare an initial commercial sketch and internal approval path for a potential PO.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Date: 2027-02-20T16:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up: usage & rate-limit clarification

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the clear next steps. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak windows: Typically bursts are short (5–30 minutes) but can last a few hours during big feature launches. We see ~1.5–2x sustained for a few hours, and rare extreme spikes that can be 3–4x for <30 minutes.
- Latency SLO: Our front-end product needs interactive responses under 800ms p95 for main flows. For lower-priority background tasks we tolerate higher latency.
- Volume certainty: We’re comfortable budgeting $8k–$20k/month initially; a realistic starting estimate is ~400M tokens/month, but we may scale toward 1B+ inside 6–12 months if adoption is strong.
- Overage mindset: We prefer predictable overage pricing and a short approval lead time for temporary quota increases (procurement can approve up to $Xk per incident if reasonably justified).

Please loop in engineering with any technical limits and a clear callout for procurement (DocuSign/PO cadence).

Best,
John
Head of Platform
Acme Corp
john.doe@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up: usage & rate-limit clarification

Thanks John — helpful detail. Looping Camila to confirm the options and to propose a recommended configuration.

A few notes on process: 
- Hosted (standard) approach: we provide an initial quota based on committed monthly tokens; short bursts are tolerated via our burst reserve but sustained traffic beyond quota triggers overage rates. Overage is billed monthly and we can set pre-approval thresholds so Procurement doesn’t need to sign off on small incidents.
- Dedicated (reserved) option: reserved throughput for predictable latency at scale — recommended if you expect sustained 1B+ tokens or strict p95 latency needs. Pricing is based on committed units plus any short-term bursts above the commit.

Camila — can you share the hosted quota baseline & overage tiers and provide an example cost calc for: baseline 400M/mo, peak 2x for 2 hours/day, and a scenario hitting 1B/mo? Also, please call out the turnaround time to bump quota for hosted customers and what we’d require from Acme during those events.

I’ll also send a DocuSign sketch for the initial commercial outline for Procurement to review.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2027-02-21T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up: usage & rate-limit clarification

Hi John / Marissa — quick technical/pricing breakdown based on the numbers above. High level options: 

1) Hosted (recommended to start)
- Baseline quota: set to match expected sustained throughput (we’d suggest 500M tokens/mo to start for the 400M estimate).
- Burst handling: short bursts are handled by a burst reserve. We allow bursts up to ~3x baseline for short windows (minutes), and up to ~2x for sustained windows of a few hours depending on region capacity. For extreme spikes we rely on pre-warming or temporary quota increases.
- Quota increases: typical turnaround is 24–72 hours for Hosted quota increases (same-day for urgent pre-approved customers); we’ll need a short incident request form and a PO/chargeable card on file for immediate increases beyond pre-approved thresholds.
- Overage pricing (hosted): tiered overage; examples below (public-facing illustration):
  - Up to baseline commit: $0 (included)
  - Tier 1 overage (baseline to 2x baseline): $12 per 1M tokens
  - Tier 2 overage (2x baseline to 5x baseline): $18 per 1M tokens
  - Emergency / on-demand (>5x baseline): case-by-case pricing / short-term Dedicated recommendation

Example cost calc (baseline 500M/mo, target $/1M = $12):
- Baseline usage 500M -> cost = 500 * $12 = $6,000
- If daily 2x peak for 2 hours (adds ~30M tokens/day -> ~900M additional tokens/month if daily; adjust based on real pattern) -> overage calculation would use Tier 1 rates for the incremental tokens. We’ll run exact math once you provide a sample week of traffic.

2) Dedicated (recommended if you hit sustained 1B+ or strict p95 < 800ms needs)
- Reserved throughput with predictable unit pricing and SLA for latency.
- Can handle large bursts naturally with reserved capacity; short-term elastic burst options available but generally pricier.

Operational notes / asks:
- To enable same-day quota increases we require: a brief traffic justification (time window + expected tokens), a billing authorization (PO or card), and a security contact for urgent access approvals.
- We can whitelist certain endpoints for higher rate limits during launches (pre-warm).

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: share one week of real traffic (sample CSV) so I can run a more accurate cost model (I see ACME-Usage-Sheet.csv attached).
- John / Procurement: confirm acceptable overage approval threshold (e.g., auto-approve up to $5k per incident).
- If clear runway to 1B in 3–6 months, we should model Dedicated vs Hosted with commit math.

Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the calc — I can prepare two scenarios (hosted with burst + overage; dedicated commit).

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai
